work_order.understanding: Of the four review findings on #16, two still reproduce and are the same defect seen twice; two no longer belong to this ticket. The live defect is that AC-3's per-database dedupe is delivered in the source but pinned by nothing: the five patterns in transaction-rules.test.ts:661 and the two in index.test.ts's volume test are each unique to their file, so a process-wide Set and a per-database Set produce identical counts, and hoisting reportedInvalidRegexps back to module scope in either file leaves the suite green (the reviewer reproduced this; I reproduced it independently on both files). The comment at index.test.ts:255 is the same gap stated as prose: it says 'the dedupe set below is scoped to this database handle', but there is no Set in that file — grep for reportedInvalidRegexps in index.test.ts returns nothing; the Sets live in index.ts:221 and index.electron.ts:131 — and it is the only place the file claims the order-independence the assertion does not have. So one fix closes both findings: a test that opens two databases in one process and expects one log per handle, which makes the comment's claim true instead of implied, and a comment that stops pointing at a Set the file does not contain. No production source changes: the guard's semantics are already correct, and the change is to make the suite able to say so.
work_order.root_cause: The dedupe set's lifetime is a property of where a variable is declared, and the tests written for it assert only observable counts over patterns unique to a single file. A per-handle Set and a process-wide Set are indistinguishable under those assertions, so the test passes under both the correct code and the reverted code — the property AC-3 is about was never made falsifiable. The comment at index.test.ts:255 then described the intended lifetime in prose, in a file that contains no Set, which is how the gap survived review.
work_order.approach:
Add one test per sqlite backend that distinguishes the two Set lifetimes, and correct the comment that misstates where the Set lives. The distinguishing assertion is the same on both sides: open two databases in one process, run the SAME broken pattern over both, expect the log count to go 1 then 2. A per-handle Set reports it twice; a module-scoped Set silences the second handle and the count stays 1. I verified this fails on both files when the Set is hoisted.

Import from the '#platform/server/sqlite' subpath instead — package.json maps it to index.electron.ts under the 'electron' condition, which is what ENV=node resolves (vitest.config.ts sets ssr.resolve.conditions to ['electron', ...]). This is the same path transaction-rules.test.ts already reaches the file by.

2. The new file lands where the node suite already collects it. vitest.config.ts excludes only 'src/platform/server/sqlite/index.test.ts', so index.electron.test.ts is picked up by ENV=node automatically, and vitest.web.config.ts has an explicit include list that does not mention it, so it runs exactly once. The sibling unicodeLike.test.ts is the precedent.

The web-side test goes in the existing index.test.ts, which is already in the web config's include list. Its helper `invalidRegexLogs` is duplicated rather than extracted: the two files run in different vitest projects with different module graphs, and a shared helper would have to live outside both.

files.change: Two changes. (1) Replace the comment at lines 255-257, which currently reads 'Patterns used by no other case in this file, and the dedupe set below is scoped to this database handle, so the count starts from an unreported pattern regardless of which tests ran before this one', with: 'Patterns used by no other case in this file, so the count starts from an unreported pattern. That each is reported exactly once is a statement about this handle's rows, not about the lifetime of the dedupe set — the Set lives in the closure createRegexp returns in ./index.ts, and the test below is what pins that lifetime.' (2) Insert a new `it` immediately after the test ending at line 299 and before 'should still match a valid regex that does match, and not throw on one that does not', named 'should report an unparseable pattern once per database handle, not once per process'. It opens two databases with `await openDatabase()` (no argument), seeds each with `execQuery(db, initSQL)` plus three rows INSERTed into textstrings with string '#mortgage note', spies console.log with `vi.spyOn(console, 'log').mockImplementation(() => null)`, and asserts the count of calls whose first argument is 'invalid regexp in sqlite REGEXP' goes 1 then 2 across `runQuery(db1, "SELECT id FROM textstrings where REGEXP('(?<handle', string)", null, true)` followed by the identical query on db2. It then repeats the db1 query and asserts the count is still 2, so each handle dedupes independently after its own first report. Use the pattern '(?<handle' — no other case in this file uses it. Restore the spy at the end.
files.why: This file is the only coverage index.ts (the browser/sql.js backend) has, and its existing assertions cannot tell a per-handle Set from a process-wide one. index.test.ts:255's comment is also finding 1: it points at 'the dedupe set below' when no Set exists in this file.

files.change: New file. It is the first direct test of index.electron.ts and exists solely to pin the dedupe Set's lifetime for the native backend. Import `{ execQuery, openDatabase, runQuery } from '#platform/server/sqlite'` — NOT from './index.electron', which the eslint/no-restricted-imports pattern '**/*.electron' in .oxlintrc.json rejects and which fails `yarn lint`. Under ENV=node that subpath resolves to index.electron.ts. Declare a module-level `const initSQL` creating `CREATE TABLE textstrings (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, string TEXT);`, and two constants PATTERN_ONE = '(?<electron-lifetime-one' and PATTERN_TWO = '(?<electron-lifetime-two', neither used anywhere else in the suite. Add a `seed(db)` helper that runs execQuery(db, initSQL) then inserts ids '1','2','3' with string '#mortgage note' — several rows, because SQLite calls the REGEXP function once per candidate row and a single-row table cannot tell per-pattern logging from per-row logging. Add a `countInvalidRegexLogs(spy)` helper returning the number of spy calls whose first argument is 'invalid regexp in sqlite REGEXP'. One `describe('Native sqlite REGEXP guard')` containing one `it('reports an unparseable pattern once per database handle, not once per process')`: open db1 = openDatabase(':memory:') and db2 = openDatabase(':memory:'), seed both, spy on console.log, assert runQuery(db1, `SELECT id FROM textstrings where REGEXP('${PATTERN_ONE}', string)`, [], true) returns [] and the count is 1; assert the identical query on db2 returns [] and the count is 2; repeat on db1 and assert the count is still 2; run PATTERN_TWO on db2 and assert 3; run the valid pattern '#mortgage' on db1 with fetchAll and assert it returns 3 rows with the count still 3. Restore the spy, then db1.close() and db2.close(). Note that this backend's runQuery takes [] for params — passing null throws 'params is not iterable'.
files.why: transaction-rules.test.ts reaches index.electron.ts only through getMatchingTransactions on a single shared handle, which is why hoisting the Set there left the suite green. The reviewer flagged exactly this and named the fix: open two databases in one process and expect one log per handle.

Evidence: packages/loot-core/tsconfig.json declares only 'paths' (hyperformula), no 'customConditions'. package.json exports['./platform/server/sqlite'] = {electron: index.electron.ts, api: index.api.ts, default: index.ts}. Confirmed by substitution: replacing './index.api' with '#platform/server/sqlite' and running tsgo produces 11 errors in the file (TS2740 BetterSqlite3.Database vs sql.js Database, TS2339 close on Promise<any>) — the default condition is what tsgo picks. The sibling precedent ../connection/index.api.test.ts carries a two-line version of the same note and no explanation of why.

Fix: Optional and outside this ticket: add "customConditions": ["electron"] to packages/loot-core/tsconfig.json so the subpath resolves to the native backend for typechecking, then the disable comment can shrink to one line. Do not do it in this PR — it changes type resolution for the whole package, which is a much larger blast radius than a test-only ticket should carry. The comment as written is correct and sufficient for now.

review.title: The web test's new case repeats the same six-line runQuery(...) call three times to run one query against three handles, where a three-line local query(db, pattern) helper would say the same thing — and the electron test written in the same PR already uses exactly that helper shape. The asymmetry is the only thing that makes the new web case 40 lines longer than its electron twin; at 3am the reader of index.test.ts has to re-read three near-identical blocks to confirm they differ only in the handle.

The asymmetry is the only thing that makes the new web case 40 lines longer than its electron twin; at 3am the reader of index.test.ts has to re-read three near-identical blocks to confirm they differ only in the handle.

`packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.test.ts:305`

Evidence: index.test.ts:334-345, 348-359, 362-373 are three verbatim blocks differing only in db1/db2, wrapping the identical "SELECT id FROM textstrings where REGEXP('(?<handle', string)" with null params. index.electron.test.ts:52-58 defines `const query = (db, pattern) => runQuery(db, `SELECT id FROM textstrings where REGEXP('${pattern}', string)`, [], true);` and every call site is one line. The web copy cannot lift that helper verbatim because it passes null params rather than [] — noted in the electron file's own comment at line 50 — but it can define the same shape with null.

Fix: Optional. Add a local `const query = (db, pattern) => runQuery(db, `SELECT id FROM textstrings where REGEXP('${pattern}', string)`, null, true);` in the new case and call it three times, mirroring index.electron.test.ts. Not required for correctness and not worth a re-push on its own; the readability gain is real but modest.
